Hi all, and welcome to AI Literacy for adults who care for children and adolescents. My name is Christina Buencamino and I will be walking you through the context, psychology, potential harms, and working solutions to harmful AI interaction amongst younger generations. The purpose of this course is to help you understand how AI works and why humans react to it in certain ways, in hopes of educating you on the full end to end relationship of a child or adolescent and their AI usage. By doing so, you may take key takeaways that can help inform how you approach AI usage in your life, your child’s life, and in the world around you.

This course has four modules, with 3 to 4 lessons each. In module 1, you will receive an introduction to the course, what generative AI is, where you and your children can find generative AI, and why it has become so widespread. In Module 2, we will go over the psychological and cognitive reasons for why people may develop harmful or dependent relationships, and why children and adolescents may be more at risk of doing so. In Module 3, we will go over the most common types of harms that can occur when a child or adolescent uses generative AI in an unsupervised way. And finally, in Module 4 we will conclude by discussing the current solutions to these issues in the world, whether they be on an educational, governmental, or global scale.

Each lesson will have a check your understanding quiz question at the end that, once completed, will take you to the next lesson. At the end of each module, you will take a module quiz to confirm your understanding of the module questions. And lastly, at the end of the course you will take a final quiz to go over everything you have learned. By the end, you should have a better understanding of how generative AI and its impact on younger generations is.

Technological innovation continues to push the boundaries of how we live and grow every day. Major breakthroughs can lead to drastic changes in how society works, creating generational gaps in life experience. While baby boomers grew up with rotary phones, generation Z was able to acquire a smart phone at a relatively young age. While millennials grew up with Blockbuster and Netflix would mail you DVDs, generation alpha has never known a time where you couldn’t stream movies online.

One of the latest technological breakthroughs that has taken the world by storm is the rise of generative AI. Generative AI, which is commonly accessed through chatbots like ChatGPT, is a form of artificial intelligence that can be trained on data in order to interpret various medias like text, and produce original content [1].While older generations experienced a childhood without these tools, younger generation alphas, generation betas, and beyond are experiencing a world where these generative AI tools have always been an accessible norm.

While generative AI continues to be embedded into more and more aspects of the world, governance and understanding have not moved at the same rate. Many have raised ethical and security concerns as generative AI continues to surface in everyday parts of life, such as in work, academia, healthcare, and common tools. These AI tools have been linked to harmful actions, such as generating voice or images to impersonate others (known as deepfakes), responding with incorrect information but presenting it as fact, and overall have a lack of accountability that makes it hard for legislation to protect the population from unintended side effects [2].

While adults can be victims of these harmful actions, further consideration must be taken for children and adolescents. Children and adolescents do not have the same experience of AI being introduced to them as adults do; they are being raised in a world where they have always known of generative AI, which can reduce the skepticism and intention behind their interactions compared to adults. Therefore, this course has been built to improve AI literacy in adult caregivers of children and adolescents, so that you may understand the nuances, psychology, and pitfalls of interactions between younger generations and AI so that you can make informed decisions and actions to protect them from potential harm.
